topic.title: Auditory Coding and Multiscale Sound Processing
topic.overview: Sound carries useful structure across many time scales, from rapid spectral changes to extended sequences. This topic studies how auditory systems and computational models encode that structure, locate sources, and separate meaningful signals from noise. Biological mechanisms motivate both models of hearing and signal-processing methods in other domains.
topic.whyItMatters: Handling several time scales simultaneously can improve sensitivity to patterns that short windows miss. However, an auditory analogy is a design motivation rather than evidence of biological equivalence, and performance in an engineering application does not establish how the nervous system performs the corresponding computation.
topic.evolution: Early representatives examine cochlear implants, analog cochleae, and song learning. Later work models auditory receptive fields and sound localization. A 2007 modulation-cascade model captures natural-sound structure across time scales; recent representatives include acoustic response fields and a 2026 battery-prediction method inspired by bilateral auditory comparisons to amplify weak degradation signals.
openQuestions: How can auditory models retain long-range structure without sacrificing temporal precision?
Which biologically motivated mechanisms transfer reliably to noisy non-audio signals?
